Notebook introduction

This document provides an exhaustive, bit-by-bit technical breakdown of the **GPU Compute Subsystem** in the Retiam WebGPU Engine. It covers the declarative user-facing [`ComputeKernel`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/compute/ComputeKernel.ts) API, low-level engine compute pipelines ([`Compute.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/compute/Compute.ts)), parallel prefix scan algorithms, marching cubes volumetric extraction, and seamless integration with the FrameGraph and hardware instancing.
1. Architectural Overview & Dual Compute Paradigms
WebGPU treats Compute Shaders as first-class citizens alongside graphics rasterization. Retiam provides **two complementary compute layers**:

children: Automatic `@group(0)` bind group layout generation and WGSL boilerplate injection via `ShaderBuilder`.
Lazy pipeline compilation with global pipeline caching (`PipelineCache`).
23+ optimized built-in kernels for geometric stroke extrusion, parallel prefix scans, 3D contour reconstruction, bezier subdivision, and morph interpolation.

C. Zero-Allocation Dispatching
When `dispatch()` is called:

items: **First Frame**: Compiles WGSL via `ShaderBuilder`, creates `GPUBindGroupLayout`, queries `PipelineCache`, and allocates `GPUBindGroup`.
**Subsequent Frames**: Returns the pre-built `ComputeCommand` with updated dispatch counts. **0.0 KB garbage collection allocations** per frame.

4. Built-In Engine Compute Kernels ([Compute.ts](../src/engine/compute/Compute.ts))
The Retiam core includes 23+ optimized GPU compute operations organized under the [`ComputeType`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/compute/Compute.ts#L35) enumeration:

cells.text: Parallel 2D ribbon mesh generation (`mesh_generator.wgsl`), end caps (`mesh_generator_ends.wgsl`), earcut polygon triangulation, and vertex normal offset displacement.
Work-efficient parallel scan (`prefix_sum.wgsl` & `prefix_copy.wgsl`) for GPU stream compaction and variable-length contour index allocation.
Evaluates dense bézier curves, Chaikin corner-cutting subdivision, linear shape morphing, and 3D Simplex noise swarm transforms (`swarm_morph.wgsl`).
High-precision numerical integration of bézier and 3D line arc lengths for screen-space invariant dash patterns and write animations.
GPU Marching Cubes iso-surface extraction (`sdf_marching_cubes.wgsl`) and Dual Contouring for real-time mathematical 3D plotting.

6. Best Practices, Workgroup Sizing & GPU Hardware Limits

children: **1D Buffers / Particles**: Use `[64, 1, 1]` or `[128, 1, 1]`. This aligns with hardware wave/warp sizes (32 on NVIDIA, 64 on AMD) and avoids thread underutilization.
**2D Textures / Images**: Use `[16, 16, 1]` or `[8, 8, 1]` ($16 \times 16 = 256$ threads per workgroup).
Storage buffer sizes and copy offsets must be multiples of **4 bytes** (32-bit aligned).
Uniform buffer bindings must align to **256 bytes** (`minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment`).
Always guard kernels with boundary checks:

blocks.code:
let idx = global_id.x;
     if (idx >= totalElementCount) { return; }

children: Use `var<workgroup> sharedData: array<f32, 64>;` for inter-thread reductions within the same workgroup.
Always call `workgroupBarrier()` to synchronize memory reads and writes across threads in a workgroup.
